confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from two web searches. Numbeo-based figures for London (via Expatica, June 2026) gave roughly £7 for a domestic draught beer, £4.1 for a cappuccino, £20 for an inexpensive meal, £81 for a three-course meal for two, and about £10 for a mid-range bottle of wine. I converted these to USD at an assumed GBP/USD of about 1.33, which I did not look up. The cocktail figure rests on an old £11 guide price, adjusted upward and set relative to beer, so it is uncertain. The wine-by-the-glass figure is derived from the bottle price and a £7-12 guide range. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for July peak season, with no listings checked. Only two of the five permitted price searches were used, and the second covered all price items at once.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on London-specific aggregated price data (Numbeo via Expatica). Accommodation is based on general knowledge of central and inner London peak-season rates.
